batches.title: R3 source governance and authority boundaries
batches.description: Current R3 guidance that constrains what may be carried into R3A and where new institutional guidance belongs.
batches.summary: The current R3 index directs new R3 runbooks to ppow1/R3, treats Riverview- as reference, and says not to migrate Riverview 2 wholesale. The approved charter requires relevant knowledge retrieval and preserves evidence provenance.
batches.conflicts_and_supersession: Legacy Riverview execution-first directions cannot override the current R3 charter or this Steward-directed review and approval requirement.
batches.recommended_disposition: Review each item; the batch has no default decision.

batches.title: External review and promotion practices
batches.description: Potentially reusable process ideas from older Riverview and Estate guidance; neither repository governs R3A.
batches.summary: Both external projects distinguish draft material from institutional authority or warn against silent promotion. These are reference ideas. R3A already requires explicit Steward authority; this batch cannot alter that rule.
batches.conflicts_and_supersession: External repository instructions are not R3A authority. Any external text conflicting with the current R3 charter or explicit Steward direction remains ineligible for bulk disposition.
batches.recommended_disposition: Defer the external adaptation for R3A policy review; review entries individually.

batches.title: Legacy and project-specific operating rules
batches.description: Examples identified during discovery that should not become current R3A knowledge without an explicit scope decision.
batches.summary: The legacy guide contains older execution-first operating language. CueMastery assigns a project-specific communication authority to Ionoge Comms7. Both demonstrate why scope and current authority must be checked before reuse.
batches.conflicts_and_supersession: The execution-first legacy instruction conflicts with explicit R3A Steward approval and non-promotion requirements. CueMastery authority is not transferable to R3A.
batches.recommended_disposition: Reject the legacy instruction as current R3A policy; defer the CueMastery item as out of scope. Both require individual review.

entries.title: Keep new R3 engineering guidance in the R3 repository
entries.summary: The R3 guidance index assigns new R3 runbooks to ppow1/R3, treats ppow1/Riverview- as historical/reference material, and rejects wholesale migration of Riverview 2.
entries.why_it_matters: Keeps new R3A operational instructions discoverable in the repository designated by current R3 guidance and prevents legacy instructions from silently becoming R3A policy.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: For new Riverview 3 engineering and operational runbooks, use ppow1/R3. Treat ppow1/Riverview- as historical/reference material and assess legacy material before any R3A adaptation.

sources.location: Runbook ownership and Essential rules, lines 30-38; line 46
sources.excerpt: All NEW Riverview 3 engineering and operational runbooks ... must be created or updated in ppow1/R3 only. ppow1/Riverview- is historical/reference material ... Do not migrate Riverview 2 wholesale.

entries.authority_assessment: Current R3 repository guidance; subordinate to approved R3 charter and roadmap. Applicable for R3A source location, subject to current owner confirmation if repository roles change.
entries.freshness: Current inspected branch index, last changed 2026-11-06.

entries.title: Residents should consult relevant existing institutional knowledge
entries.summary: The approved R3 charter requires residents to consult relevant existing knowledge before independently investigating or acting and to preserve evidence and provenance for verified facts.
entries.why_it_matters: Makes retrieval a normal part of resident work and reduces repeated rediscovery while retaining source lineage.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: When relevant institutional knowledge exists, residents consult it before independent investigation or action. Verified facts retain evidence and provenance; binding rules retain scope and authority.

sources.location: Institutional knowledge and grounding, section 5, lines 68-72
sources.excerpt: Every resident shall consult relevant existing knowledge before independently investigating or acting ... Verified facts shall retain evidence and provenance; binding rules shall retain scope and authority.

entries.authority_assessment: Current authoritative R3 charter; Steward approval is recorded in the source document.
entries.freshness: Approved 2026-10-31; checked against current R3A knowledge contract and roadmap on 2026-11-08.

entries.title: Keep evidence, inference, uncertainty, and fiction distinct
entries.summary: The R3 charter requires residents to distinguish verified claims from inference, unknowns, fictional improvisation, and operational observation; retrieval or citation alone is not proof.
entries.why_it_matters: A retrieved passage is evidence for Grace to interpret, not an automatic decision or proof that every adjacent claim is true.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: Residents label claims according to their support. Retrieval and citations are not themselves proof; preserve the evidence pointers and distinguish inference and uncertainty from verified institutional facts.

sources.excerpt: Retrieval and citation are not themselves proof: evidence must actually support the specific claim. Residents shall explicitly acknowledge uncertainty and distinguish inference from fact.

entries.freshness: Approved 2026-10-31; no superseding charter identified in inspected R3 guidance.

entries.title: Keep proposal review separate from institutional promotion
entries.summary: Riverview- guidance says a proposal draft is not execution authority and distinguishes Steward approval from a separately authorized promotion step.
entries.why_it_matters: This separation may help keep discovery and proposal generation from becoming an implicit authority path in R3A.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: Candidate wording for review only: a generated knowledge proposal remains non-authoritative until the designated Steward decision and established authorized promotion operation are recorded.

sources.location: Proposal and approval guidance; repository scope section
sources.excerpt: Proposal drafts are not execution authority; use the documented authenticated Steward flow; approval and separately authorized promotion are distinct.

entries.authority_assessment: Historical/reference guidance from a separate Riverview repository; adaptation requires R3A owner review. Current R3 charter and this Steward directive independently require explicit authority.
entries.freshness: File modified 2026-10-22; verify against current source before any future ingestion.

entries.title: Do not silently promote AI classifications into canonical knowledge
entries.summary: Estate software-development guidance allows AI systems to propose, classify, summarize, and identify gaps, but says they do not silently promote canonical knowledge or alter accepted baselines.
entries.why_it_matters: This is a candidate design principle for keeping the batch tool advisory and approval-controlled.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: Candidate adaptation only: discovery and classification may prepare review proposals; promotion requires the established R3A Steward approval and authorized ingestion path.

sources.location: AI services and governance guidance, lines 158 onward
sources.excerpt: Local AI may propose, classify, summarize, and identify gaps, but does not silently promote canonical knowledge or alter accepted baselines.

entries.title: Legacy execution-first instruction is not current R3A policy

entries.why_it_matters: Makes a known conflict visible so a future reader does not mistake a legacy repository instruction for current R3A authority.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: Historical note: do not apply Riverview legacy execution-first wording to R3A knowledge promotion; current R3A decisions follow the approved R3 charter and explicit Steward direction.

entries.title: CueMastery communications authority is project-specific
entries.summary: CueMastery guidance assigns communications authority in that project to Ionoge Comms7. It provides no R3A resident or institutional authority.
entries.why_it_matters: Captures the scope check and avoids importing unrelated project identities or authority structures into R3A.
entries.proposed_canonical_knowledge: Do not import CueMastery or Ionoge authority assignments into R3A; consult R3A's own approved charter, roster, and contracts.
